originalTitle: Venezuelan leader marks Independence Day with message of ‘no social unrest’
title: Venezuela's Brave Helpers!
content:
Hello, my awesome friends in Africa! It's your kid-friendly news reporter, here to share a story from a country far, far away called Venezuela. Imagine a beautiful place with lots of sunshine and happy people. Sometimes, even in sunny places, big things can happen. Let's talk about a big shake and how everyone helped each other.

A Big Shake in Venezuela

On June 24th, something called an earthquake happened in Venezuela. An earthquake is when the ground underneath us starts to shake and rumble. It's like the Earth is doing a little dance! Sometimes, this dance can be very strong, and it can make buildings wiggle and things fall over. It can be a little scary when it happens. **Did you know?** Earthquakes happen when big pieces of the Earth's crust (like puzzle pieces!) move and rub against each other. It's totally natural, but it can make a big rumble! When the ground shook on June 24th, some houses and buildings were hurt. People needed help. Imagine if your toy tower suddenly tumbled down – you'd need a helping hand to build it back up, right? That's what happened in Venezuela, but with real houses.

Friends Helping Friends

But guess what? Even when big shakes happen, people are super brave and kind! In Venezuela, everyone jumped in to help each other. Neighbours helped neighbours, friends helped friends, and even strangers lent a hand. They made sure everyone was safe and had what they needed. People shared food, gave warm blankets, and offered hugs. They showed that even when things are tough, being kind and helping each other makes everything better. It's like when your friend falls, and you help them up – that's what Venezuela did, but on a much bigger scale! **Did you know?** When people help each other after a big problem, it's called community spirit! It means everyone in a town or city works together like a big family.

Leaders Share How They Helped

Now, a leader in Venezuela, a lady named Delcy Rodriguez, spoke about what happened. She talked about how the leaders and the government worked very hard to help everyone after the big earthquake. They sent out teams to find people who needed help. They made sure doctors and nurses were there to take care of anyone who was hurt. They also sent food, water, and special kits to help people who couldn't stay in their homes. It's like when your teachers and parents make sure you are safe and have everything you need. The leaders in Venezuela did their very best to look after their people. **Did you know?** Governments in countries are like big helpers! They have jobs to keep everyone safe, build roads, and make sure schools are open. It's a very important job! Leader Delcy Rodriguez wanted everyone to know that they were doing everything they could. She wanted people to feel safe and cared for. She shared the good news that people were staying calm and working together. This is very important because when everyone helps, things get better much faster.

Building Back Stronger

After the big shake, people in Venezuela didn't give up! They started to clean up and rebuild. It's like putting the pieces of a puzzle back together. Builders, engineers, and everyday people all worked side by side. They showed how strong and determined they are. They are working to make their homes and towns even stronger than before. Imagine building a sandcastle, and then a wave knocks it down. Do you give up? No! You start building it again, maybe even bigger and better! That's the spirit of the people in Venezuela. **Did you know?** Many countries around the world send help and support to places that have experienced earthquakes. It's a way of showing that we are all one big global family!

A Special Day for Venezuela

This special message from the leader came during a very important time for Venezuela. It was their Independence Day! Independence Day is a super special holiday when a country celebrates being free and choosing its own way. It's like a big birthday party for the whole country! On Independence Day, people usually celebrate with parades, music, and lots of joy. Even after the earthquake, the message was about hope, strength, and working together. It was a day to remember that even through hard times, they are a strong and united country. **Did you know?** Just like Venezuela, many countries in Africa also celebrate their Independence Day! It's a day to be proud of your country and its history.

What We Learn

So, what can we learn from our friends in Venezuela? We learn that even when unexpected things happen, like a big earthquake, people can be incredibly brave and kind. We learn that helping hands make problems smaller. And we learn that working together, like a big team, makes us all stronger. It's a wonderful reminder that no matter where we live, being a good friend and helping others is one of the most important things we can do. From your friends here in Africa, we send big hugs and cheers to the brave people of Venezuela! **Did you know?** Even small acts of kindness, like sharing your toys or helping a friend with their homework, can make a huge difference!
summary: A leader in Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, shared how the government and kind people worked together to help everyone after a big earthquake on June 24th, showing courage and teamwork on their special Independence Day.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows that even when big problems like earthquakes happen, people can be very brave, kind, and work together to help each other and make things better.
